AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit.

2. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 50 °C

3. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only water vapour

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preparation of Animal Products? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preparation of Animal Products.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preparation of Animal Products.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preparation of Animal Products.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Preparation of Animal Products.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preserving Animal Products 9 2.6 Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygie? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preserving Animal Products 9 2.6 Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygie.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preserving Animal Products 9 2.6 Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygie.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preserving Animal Products 9 2.6 Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygie.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Preserving Animal Products 9 2.6 Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygie.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Soil Conservation Measures? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Conservation Measures.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Soil Conservation Measures.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Soil Conservation Measures.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Soil Conservation Measures.

7. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Heating until a solid melts

8. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A mixture of two liquids

9. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Pest and Disease Control? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Pest and Disease Control.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Pest and Disease Control.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Pest and Disease Control.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Pest and Disease Control.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cleaning the Kitchen? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cleaning the Kitchen.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cleaning the Kitchen.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cleaning the Kitchen.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Cleaning the Kitchen.

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Harvesting and Storage? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Harvesting and Storage.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Harvesting and Storage.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Water Harvesting and Storage.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Harvesting and Storage.

14. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cleaning the Kitchen 9 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Sewing Skills: Constructing? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cleaning the Kitchen 9 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Sewing Skills: Constructing.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cleaning the Kitchen 9 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Sewing Skills: Constructing.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Cleaning the Kitchen 9 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Sewing Skills: Constructing.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cleaning the Kitchen 9 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Sewing Skills: Constructing.

16. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Overgrazing continuously

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Preserving animal products and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Cleaning the Kitchen and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Sewing Skills: Constructing Household Items 14 4.2 Constructing Innovative Anima and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
